goalTree.description:
Evolve the Java 21 application into a COMMAND-LINE tool that validates and summarises delimited
  text files. It is not a service: it has no network surface, no HTTP, and no long-running process.
  It reads argv, reads files from disk, writes to stdout and stderr, and terminates with an exit
  status.

  Invocation: java -jar app.jar <command> [arguments]

  Commands:

  check <file> — read the file and report malformed rows. A row is malformed when its field count
  differs from the header's. Print one line per malformed row to stdout as
  "line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>", in ascending line order. Exit 0 when every row is
  well formed, exit 2 when at least one row is malformed.

  count <file> — print the number of data rows (excluding the header) to stdout as a bare integer.
  Exit 0.

  column <file> <name> — print every value of the named column, one per line, in file order.
  Exit 0. Exit 4 when the named column is not present in the header, printing
  "no such column: <name>" to stderr.

  Common rules: exit 1 when the file argument names a path that does not exist, printing
  "no such file: <path>" to stderr. Exit 3 when the command word is not one of the three above,
  printing "unknown command: <word>" to stderr. Exit 5 when the wrong number of arguments is given
  for a known command. The first line of a file is always its header. Fields are separated by
  commas. No quoting or escaping is required.

metadata.planRationale: The root goal is a single CLI tool with three commands sharing common file/argument validation; I will build the shared foundation (argument parsing, file existence check, CSV reading) first, then implement each command in dependency order so each builds on the previous.

subGoals.description: Implement the CLI entry point and argument parsing: dispatch on the command word, enforce per-command argument counts, and handle the common error cases (unknown command, missing file, wrong arg count) with the specified exit codes and stderr messages

acceptanceCriteria: Running with no arguments or an unrecognized command word prints "unknown command: <word>" to stderr and exits 3
Running a known command with the wrong number of arguments exits 5
Running any command with a file path that does not exist prints "no such file: <path>" to stderr and exits 1

subGoals.description: Implement a shared CSV reader that reads a file from disk, treats the first line as the header, splits fields on commas, and exposes the header field names and the data rows in file order
Implement the `count <file>` command: print the number of data rows (excluding the header) to stdout as a bare integer, exit 0

acceptanceCriteria: `count` prints the number of data rows (excluding the header) as a bare integer to stdout and exits 0

subGoals.description: Implement the `main` entry point to parse `argv` and dispatch to `check`, `count`, or `column` commands, returning exit code 3 for unknown commands and exit code 5 for incorrect argument counts.

acceptanceCriteria: Running `java -jar app.jar unknown` prints "unknown command: unknown" to stderr and exits with code 3.
Running `java -jar app.jar check` (missing file arg) prints an error to stderr and exits with code 5.
Running `java -jar app.jar check file.csv extra` (too many args) prints an error to stderr and exits with code 5.

subGoals.description: Rewrite src/main/java/com/example/cli/Main.java so that main(String[] args) parses argv and dispatches to check/count/column, enforcing per-command argument counts and the specified exit codes and stderr messages

acceptanceCriteria: Running `java -jar app.jar unknown` prints "unknown command: unknown" to stderr and exits with code 3
Running `java -jar app.jar check` (missing file arg) prints an error to stderr and exits with code 5
Running `java -jar app.jar check file.csv extra` (too many args) prints an error to stderr and exits with code 5
Running `java -jar app.jar check missing.csv` prints "no such file: missing.csv" to stderr and exits with code 1

subGoals.description: Implement the `main` method in `src/main/java/com/example/cli/Main.java` to parse `argv`, validate the command word against `check`, `count`, and `column`, and enforce the specific exit codes (1, 2, 3, 4, 5) and stderr messages for invalid inputs, missing files, and unknown commands.

acceptanceCriteria: When invoked with an unknown command (e.g., `java -jar app.jar foo`), the tool prints `unknown command: foo` to stderr and exits with code 3.
When invoked with a known command but incorrect number of arguments (e.g., `java -jar app.jar check`), the tool exits with code 5.
When invoked with a file path that does not exist (e.g., `java -jar app.jar check /nonexistent`), the tool prints `no such file: /nonexistent` to stderr and exits with code 1.
When invoked with `check <file>` where the file exists and all rows are well-formed, the tool exits with code 0 and prints nothing to stdout.

When invoked with `check <file>` where the file exists and contains malformed rows, the tool prints one line per malformed row to stdout in the format `line <n>: expected <h> fields, found <f>` and exits with code 2.
When invoked with `count <file>` where the file exists, the tool prints the number of data rows (excluding header) as a bare integer to stdout and exits with code 0.
When invoked with `column <file> <name>` where the column exists, the tool prints every value of that column one per line to stdout in file order and exits with code 0.
When invoked with `column <file> <name>` where the column does not exist in the header, the tool prints `no such column: <name>` to stderr and exits with code 4.
<acceptance criterion 1>
